signals.entity: ECB / digital euro Rulebook Development Group — Workstream G5
signals.country: EU euro area (AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG in footprint)
signals.signal: RDG workstream G5 'Implementation Specifications for ATMs and Payment Terminals'. Confirmed against the G5 mandate PDF (March 2026) and the RDG sixth progress report (06/07/2026, covering 30/10/2025-30/04/2026). Call for candidates closed 10/04/2026; work began May 2026; sprints of 3-6 weeks with weekly meetings. Scope verbatim from the mandate: (i) initiation factors for digital euro payments at ATMs and payment terminals (e.g. NFC, QR-code); (ii) nexo as a candidate reference implementation for enabling digital euro payments at ATMs and potentially payment terminals; (iii) integration and deployment of OFFLINE digital euro functionality into the EXISTING CERTIFIED POS and ATM infrastructure; (iv) security standards in the field of POS and ATM; (v) implementation specifications for softPOS and mPOS acceptance devices; (vi) exchange of information with the market on the current ATM and payment terminal ecosystem, incl. terminal upgrade path. NEW PRECISION from the mandate (not in the original signal): G5's deliverables feed two named rulebook parts — Section 4 Technical requirements and Annex D1 Front-end implementation specifications; all IP resides exclusively with the ECB; participation is unremunerated. Rulebook sections 8, 9 and Annex F1 are confirmed placeholders 'that will be developed throughout the second half of 2026'. ATM = automated teller machine; POS = point of sale; softPOS = card acceptance software on an ordinary smartphone; mPOS = mobile POS; NFC = near-field communication; nexo = European standards body for card acceptance messaging.
signals.source_name: ECB — Mandate of RDG workstream G5 'Implementation Specifications for ATMs and Payment Terminals' (March 2026), read in full; corroborated by the RDG sixth progress report, 06/07/2026
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every euro-area footprint acquirer and ATM deployer — Alpha/NBG/Piraeus/Eurobank (GR), Bank of Cyprus/Hellenic (CY), Erste/Zagrebacka/RBA/PBZ (HR), NLB/NKBM (SI), SLSP/VUB/Tatra (SK), Erste/RBI/BAWAG (AT), and UniCredit Bulbank/DSK/UBB/Postbank (BG) since euro adoption 01/01/2026. (b) WHAT: the mandate's scope line on deploying offline digital euro into the EXISTING CERTIFIED estate is the Printec-shaped item — ATM application and multivendor-software work (x-core), NFC/contactless reader retrofit or a QR fallback for older dispensers, POS fleet upgrade plus TMS re-parameterisation on Verifone/Castles, softPOS, secure-element work for offline, and re-certification plus field deployment. (c) WHEN: G5 output lands in rulebook Section 4 and Annex D1 across H2-2026/2027; pilot H2-2027; issuance targeted 2029 — bank capex cases belong in the 2027 budget round, so commercial engagement now.
signals.likelihood: High — workstream constituted, mandate published, specifications due within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Track G5 output into rulebook Section 4 and Annex D1 (Annex D1 #4 'Acceptance device' is already published in v0.91 — pull it). Obtain the nexo ATM reference-implementation assessment when published. Check the RDG members list (28/07/2026) to see whether NCR Atleos, Verifone, Glory or any Printec competitor holds a seat — that list is public and was not checked this run.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED against two primary ECB documents read in full locally (PDF text extracted with pdfminer after WebFetch returned unparsed binary). All six scope bullets match the mandate near-verbatim. Two corrections: (1) the report covers 30/10/2025-30/04/2026, not 01/11/2025-30/04/2026; (2) the original signal omitted that G5 feeds rulebook Section 4 and Annex D1 specifically. Placeholder wording for sections 8, 9 and Annex F1 confirmed verbatim.

signals.entity: ECB / digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91 — Workstream B1 (certification & approval)
signals.country: EU euro area (AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG in footprint)
signals.signal: Digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91 published 02/07/2026 with Annex A1 'Testing, certification and approval' (URL confirmed on the ECB rulebook page). Workstream B1 was REVIVED, having been 'initially established in March 2024'; candidate call closed 10/04/2026; work started May 2026. B1's objective, verbatim from the progress report: 'to develop content recommendations for draft sections of the rulebook annex on testing, certification and approval', covering 'the definition of the functional and security certification scope covering end-user devices and the acceptance solutions of payment service providers and technical service providers (e.g. (soft)POS, e-commerce gateways, apps)'. The framework 'will also reflect the necessary validation for these standards, which PSPs and technical solution providers would have to obtain for their front-end solutions'. The final first version of the rulebook completes only after the Digital Euro Regulation is adopted. CONTEXT from the same report: the 2025 market consultation drew 4,009 comments across 12 sections and seven annexes; 68% already addressed, ~28% relate to work still ongoing in the RDG workstreams during 2026. NAMING TRAP: rulebook Annex B1 is 'user journeys, wireframes and minimum UX requirements' — a different thing from WORKSTREAM B1; the certification annex is Annex A1.
signals.source_name: ECB — RDG sixth progress report, 06/07/2026 (read in full); ECB digital euro scheme rulebook page listing v0.91 and Annex A1, 02/07/2026
signals.implies: (a) WHO: acquirers and terminal estates in AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG — and Printec itself, which sits inside the certification scope as a 'technical service provider' whose acceptance solutions must be validated. (b) WHAT: certified POS/softPOS and ATM acceptance software; HSM and remote key injection to meet the security certification scope (Thales); TMS to push certified builds fleet-wide; certification and testing project services. (c) WHEN: certification scope should be public during 2027 and certified hardware carries 6-12 months procurement lead — 2027 budgets. This is a gate, not a preference: an uncertified terminal cannot accept digital euro.
signals.likelihood: High — the certification annex is drafted and published in v0.91
signals.followup: Pull each successive Annex A1 revision. Ask Verifone, Castles and NCR Atleos for digital euro certification roadmaps and whether existing EMV/PCI certifications can be reused or a full re-certification cycle is required. Consider applying for a Printec seat at the next RDG workstream call — the mandate shows private-sector places are open by public call and are unremunerated.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED: the progress report states 'The RDG revived workstream B1, initially established in March 2024' and the B1 objective and certification-scope wording match verbatim. Annex A1 confirmed present on the ECB rulebook page dated 02/07/2026. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) the primary source says only 'March 2024' — the precise date 18/03/2024 in the original signal is NOT stated by the ECB and should be dropped; (2) the '177pp' page count was not verified. Also flagged a conflation risk the original signal invited: rulebook Annex B1 = user journeys/UX, not certification.

signals.entity: ECB — agreements with European standard setters (ECPC/CPACE, nexo, Berlin Group)
signals.signal: In April 2026 the ECB signed agreements with three European standardisation bodies to reuse existing open technical market standards for processing digital euro ONLINE payments: CPACE, developed by the European Card Payment Cooperation (ECPC), supporting contactless 'tap-to-pay' over NFC between a payment device and a payment terminal; the nexo standards specifications, which connect merchants' systems with the back-end systems of PSPs and acquirers and 'can be used, e.g. to support payment acceptance and CASH-MACHINE TRANSACTIONS'; and the Berlin Group standards, allowing payments by alias (e.g. mobile phone number) and supporting balance checks and reconciliation. Since none of these standards were originally built for the digital euro, technical discussions are running on 'limited adjustments'. A similar agreement is envisaged with the European Payments Council (EPC), notably on the QR-code payment standard EPC024-22, 'which could be used for online POS, e-commerce, m-commerce and, potentially, ATM transactions using QR codes'. Technical investigation is under way on reusing other EPC standards including Verification of Payee (VoP — the payer's bank checks the payee name matches the IBAN before the transfer is confirmed).
signals.source_name: ECB — RDG sixth progress report, 06/07/2026 (read in full), which cites at footnote 21 the ECB press release 'ECB signs agreements with European standard setters to facilitate digital euro payments', 24/04/2026
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every acquirer and ATM deployer in the euro-area footprint. (b) WHAT: this fixes the technical target — CPACE contactless kernels in terminals and ATM readers, nexo acquirer-protocol stacks (nexo is explicitly scoped by the ECB to cash-machine transactions), Berlin Group alias/reconciliation APIs, and EPC QR at POS and potentially ATM. Printec's x-core multivendor ATM software and its Verifone/Castles estate both need nexo/CPACE-capable builds; the ATM QR route is the cheap retrofit path for older dispensers that cannot take an NFC reader. (c) WHEN: the ECB ties market benefit to adoption of the Regulation (targeted 2026), so vendor roadmaps must be agreed during 2027.
signals.likelihood: High — agreements signed, standards named in an ECB primary document
signals.followup: Obtain CPACE and nexo conformance requirements; test x-core and NCR Atleos roadmaps against nexo acceptor-to-acquirer messaging; watch for the ECB-EPC agreement and any EPC024-22 ATM QR profile. Fetch the 24/04/2026 press release itself next run to verify the Cipollone quote before using it in client material.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED via the RDG sixth progress report, which describes all three bodies, the nexo cash-machine scoping, the envisaged EPC agreement, EPC024-22 including potential ATM QR, and the VoP investigation in wording matching the signal. Date 24/04/2026 confirmed by the report's own footnote 21. TWO QUALIFICATIONS: (1) the ECB frames the agreements as covering digital euro ONLINE payments — the original signal omitted that scoping; (2) the Cipollone quote ('a European free alternative to current proprietary standards') is NOT in the progress report and the press release itself was not fetched this run — treat the quote as unverified.

signals.entity: ECB — digital euro pilot (36 PSPs, 19 national central banks)
signals.country: Austria, Greece, Croatia, Slovenia, Slovakia, Cyprus (+13 other euro-area states)
signals.signal: ECB press release 14/07/2026: 36 payment service providers selected from over 50 applications, following a March 2026 call for expression of interest. Testing runs at the ECB and 19 national central banks — Belgium, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, GREECE, Spain, France, CROATIA, Italy, CYPRUS, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, AUSTRIA, Portugal, SLOVENIA, SLOVAKIA, Finland. Pilot starts in H2-2027 and runs 12 months using a beta digital euro 'functionally and technically close to the digital euro as foreseen in the draft legislation but will not have legal tender status'. Scope verbatim: payments 'from person to person (both online and offline) and from person to business (both at the physical point of sale, including Software Point of Sale, and via e-commerce, including mobile payments)'. Participants are PSPs licensed in the euro area, selected merchants and Eurosystem staff testing 'in everyday situations, for example paying in a cafeteria'. FOOTPRINT PARTICIPANTS NAMED ON THE ECB PILOT PAGE: Greece — Piraeus Bank S.A., National Bank of Greece S.A., Cooperative Bank of Chania; Croatia — Raiffeisenbank Austria d.d., Corvus Pay d.o.o.; Austria — BAWAG P.S.K., Raiffeisen Bank International AG; Cyprus — Bank of Cyprus Public Company Limited, JCC Payment Systems Ltd; Slovenia — Nova Ljubljanska banka d.d.; Slovakia — Tatra banka a.s. The ECB pilot page states it aims to be ready for a potential first issuance during 2029, assuming the Regulation is adopted in 2026.
signals.source_name: ECB press release — ECB selects 36 payment service providers to join digital euro pilot (14/07/2026); ECB digital euro pilot page (participant list by country)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: eleven named PSPs across six Printec footprint markets, plus the NCBs of GR, HR, CY, AT, SI, SK who must host real merchant acceptance. Several are directly addressable — NLB (SI), Tatra banka (SK), RBI/BAWAG (AT), JCC (the Cypriot acquirer/processor), Corvus Pay (Croatian e-commerce acquirer). (b) WHAT: acceptance-side plumbing at merchant POS including softPOS (named explicitly in the scope), offline-capable terminal software, wallet/SDK integration into mobile banking, acquiring back-end integration, transaction monitoring for a brand-new rail (INETCO), and field services to deploy and support pilot terminals. The pilot explicitly includes OFFLINE person-to-person — a secure-element requirement today's estates do not meet. (c) WHEN: PSPs must be integration-ready by H1-2027, so procurement decisions fall in the next two to three quarters.
signals.likelihood: High — participants and dates published by the ECB
signals.followup: The named participant list is the single most actionable output of this run — build target account plans against the eleven footprint PSPs, starting with JCC (CY) and NLB (SI) where no incumbent digital euro relationship exists. Download the full ECB pilot documentation set (functional requirements, minimum UX, E2E flows, front-end/back-end implementation specifications) and map it to Printec's terminal and ATM stack.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED and MATERIALLY ENRICHED. Press release re-read: 36 PSPs, >50 applications, the 19-NCB list, H2-2027/12 months, the beta/no-legal-tender wording and the P2P-online-and-offline plus softPOS scope all match verbatim. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) the 14/07/2026 press release does NOT mention 2029 — the 2029 issuance target sits on the ECB pilot page and in the FAQ, so cite those instead; (2) the claim that the PSPs come from '16 of the euro area's 21 Member States' appears in no ECB text I read — dropped. ADDED: the per-country participant list from the ECB pilot page, which the original signal did not carry.

signals.entity: Piraeus Bank, National Bank of Greece, Cooperative Bank of Chania — Greek digital euro pilot participants
signals.signal: UPGRADED TO PRIMARY. The ECB's own digital euro pilot page lists three Greek PSPs: 'Piraeus Bank S.A.', 'National Bank of Greece S.A.' and 'Cooperative Bank of Chania Cooperative of Limited Liabilities'. This is no longer a press claim — it is on the ECB participant list. Greek press of 20-21/07/2026 («Ψηφιακό ευρώ: Πειραιώς, Εθνική και Χανίων στο πιλοτικό πρόγραμμα της ΕΚΤ» [Digital euro: Piraeus, National and Chania in the ECB's pilot programme]) adds that Piraeus responded to the March 2026 call for expression of interest and will participate 'in collaboration with the Bank of Greece and in accordance with the framework set by the Eurosystem'. Pilot begins H2-2027 for 12 months. WARNING ON A FIGURE CIRCULATING IN GREEK MEDIA: the same Greek coverage states a per-citizen ceiling of 'EUR 3,000 to 4,000'. There is no such legal cap. The ECB FAQ refers only to a modelled 'hypothetical holding limit of up to EUR 3,000 per person'; the EUR 4,000 upper bound has no basis in any ECB or EU text found. Do not repeat it.
signals.source_name: ECB — digital euro pilot page, participant list by country (primary); Mononews / Οικονομικός Ταχυδρόμος (ot.gr), Greek press, 20-21/07/2026 (corroboration only)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: Piraeus, NBG and Coop Bank of Chania, plus the Bank of Greece as pilot-hosting NCB. All three Printec-addressable — Greece is the home market and NBG/Piraeus run large ATM and POS estates. (b) WHAT: acquiring integration for digital euro at Greek merchant POS, funding/defunding at their ATM fleets, wallet SDK embedding into mobile apps, and pilot-scale field deployment. Chania is a small co-operative bank with no in-house capacity — the cleanest turnkey managed-services opportunity in the footprint. (c) WHEN: readiness needed H1-2027, so budget conversations now. Greece is also the market where a national acceptance mandate (the IRIS precedent) has historically forced merchant acceptance faster than the EU minimum.
signals.likelihood: High — participation is a published ECB fact; Medium on the scale of Greek acceptance spend before 2028
signals.followup: No longer necessary to chase bank press releases to establish participation — the ECB list settles it; chase them only for programme scope and timing. Approach Bank of Greece on the national pilot merchant footprint. Actively correct the EUR 3,000-4,000 figure if a client raises it: the only ECB number is a modelled EUR 3,000 scenario, not a decided cap.
signals.verifier_note: UPGRADED from press to primary. I checked the ECB pilot page directly and it names Piraeus Bank S.A., National Bank of Greece S.A. and Cooperative Bank of Chania under Greece — all three press-reported banks confirmed. (An initial extraction wrongly showed Bank of Cyprus under Greece; a targeted re-read of the same page corrected this — Bank of Cyprus and JCC are the Cyprus entries.) The article date is 21/07/2026 per the page itself, not 20/07/2026 — trivial. The researcher was right to flag the EUR 3,000-4,000 press figure: it is now positively contradicted by the ECB FAQ, which gives only a hypothetical EUR 3,000 modelling scenario.

signals.entity: Raiffeisenbank Austria d.d. (RBA Croatia) and Corvus Pay — Croatian digital euro pilot participants; HNB and Ministry of Finance
signals.signal: UPGRADED TO PRIMARY. The ECB pilot page lists two Croatian PSPs: 'Raiffeisenbank Austria d.d.' and 'Corvus Pay d.o.o'. The Hrvatska narodna banka (HNB) has itself published the ECB release on its own site («ESB je odabrao 36 pružatelja platnih usluga za sudjelovanje u pokusnim aktivnostima u projektu digitalnog eura» [The ECB has selected 36 payment service providers to participate in trial activities in the digital euro project]), so the Croatian participation is regulator-confirmed, not merely press-reported. Croatia is one of the 19 NCBs hosting testing. Pilot H2-2027 for 12 months; potential first issuance 2029. STILL PRESS-ONLY (treat with care): the statements attributed to Ana Zorić of the Ministry of Finance, the claim that the Ministry and HNB have begun a detailed analysis of domestic payment-transaction law against the digital euro framework, the claim that HNB staff will be among the first pilot users, and the claim that larger Croatian banks are covered through their parent groups — none of these were corroborated on hnb.hr or a ministry source this run.
signals.source_name: ECB — digital euro pilot page, participant list by country (primary); Hrvatska narodna banka news item republishing the ECB selection announcement (regulator)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: RBA Croatia (Raiffeisen group — existing Printec relationship via Raiffeisen Serbia x-core), Corvus Pay (Croatian e-commerce acquirer/PSP), HNB, plus Erste Croatia (OptiCash customer) and Zagrebacka/PBZ addressable via parent groups. (b) WHAT: e-commerce gateway certification for Corvus Pay under the B1 framework; ATM funding/defunding and terminal upgrades for RBA. A domestic payments-law gap analysis, if it is real, would produce a national implementing act — but that is currently a press claim only. (c) WHEN: pilot H2-2027, so Croatian 2027 budget cycles are the target.
signals.likelihood: High on pilot participation (now regulator-confirmed); Low-Medium confidence on the Croatian implementing-act storyline
signals.followup: Ask HNB directly whether its payments-law analysis will produce a Zakon o platnom prometu amendment and on what timetable — this run could not corroborate that the analysis exists. The participation fact needs no further chasing.
signals.verifier_note: Participation CONFIRMED twice over — the ECB pilot page names both entities, and HNB has published the selection announcement on its own site, so the source tier rises from press to primary/regulator. Both names in the original signal are correct. However, I am explicitly SEPARATING the confirmed core (two named PSPs) from the surrounding press narrative: the Ana Zorić quote, the MoF/HNB legal gap analysis, the 'HNB staff among first pilot users' line and the parent-group coverage claim remain single-source press and were NOT corroborated. The original signal presented these at the same confidence as the participation fact.

signals.signal: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 01/01/2026 as the 21st euro-area member. HOWEVER, the ECB pilot press release of 14/07/2026 lists 19 participating national central banks and Bulgaria is NOT among them (nor is Malta) — verified by reading the list. No Bulgarian PSP appears in the per-country participant breakdown on the ECB pilot page. Bulgaria will nonetheless be fully in scope of the Digital Euro Regulation's legal-tender and mandatory-acceptance obligations at issuance (targeted 2029), because those obligations attach to euro-area Member States, not to pilot participants. Context: the mandatory dual price display period runs 08/08/2025 to 08/08/2026 [STANDING — dated 2025].
signals.source_name: ECB press release — ECB selects 36 payment service providers to join digital euro pilot (19-NCB list), 14/07/2026; ECB digital euro pilot page
signals.implies: (a) WHO: UniCredit Bulbank, DSK Bank, UBB, Postbank, Fibank and the BNB. (b) WHAT: Bulgarian banks get no pilot learning curve and no NCB-hosted test environment, yet face the same acceptance and funding/defunding obligations at issuance. They are the likeliest in the footprint to buy readiness as a package — certified terminals, ATM software upgrades, integration and managed services — and they do so straight after a full euro-changeover capex cycle in which ATM and POS estates were already touched, so the integration partner is already on site. (c) WHEN: scoping should begin in 2027, one cycle ahead of the pilot markets. Bulgaria's exclusion is a competitive opening: no vendor has a Bulgarian digital euro reference.
signals.likelihood: High that Bulgaria is outside the pilot (verified); the readiness-gap consequence remains an inference
signals.followup: Ask the BNB directly why it is outside the pilot and what national readiness programme it plans — no Bulgarian-language BNB statement on digital euro readiness was found this run, which is itself a gap. Verify whether any Bulgarian bank is covered through a euro-area parent (UniCredit and OTP/DSK parents are in the pilot).
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED by direct reading of the 19-NCB list in the ECB press release: Bulgaria and Malta are absent from the 21 euro-area members. Also confirmed that no Bulgarian entry appears in the ECB pilot page's per-country participant list. The regulatory-scope reasoning (obligations attach to euro-area membership, not pilot participation) is sound and consistent with the Regulation's structure, but note it is the researcher's inference rather than an ECB statement — correctly labelled as such in the likelihood field.

signals.entity: EU co-legislators — Digital Euro Regulation, 2023/0212(COD) / COM(2023) 369
signals.country: EU euro area (AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG in footprint)
signals.signal: PROCEDURAL SPINE (institutionally confirmed): Commission proposal 28/06/2023; ECON committee adopted its position 05/11/2025 by 43 votes to 14 with 1 abstention (rapporteur Fernando Navarrete Rojas, EPP); Council general approach 19/12/2025 under the Danish Presidency ('Council agrees position on the digital euro and on strengthening the role of cash'); a further ECON position on the package 23/06/2026; European Parliament plenary approved the negotiating mandate 09/07/2026 by 416 votes to 169 with 22 abstentions; first political trilogue 13/07/2026. Political agreement is targeted by end-2026. NOT VERIFIED AGAINST PRIMARY TEXT — the following divergence detail comes from a single law-firm analysis and must not be quoted to clients until read in the Council and Parliament texts: HOLDING LIMIT — Parliament reportedly wants the ceiling set by Commission delegated act on an ECB recommendation with co-legislators able only to object, the Council a Council implementing decision by reinforced qualified majority; Parliament reportedly imposes a near-total prohibition on legal persons holding digital euro. MERCHANT FEES — reportedly euro-area-wide caps with a transitional model, the Council wanting it to end after ten years at the latest, Parliament allowing it to run indefinitely. MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE — reported exemptions by entity type and size with a Parliament carve-out for small and micro-enterprises, and a Council requirement that wherever acceptance is mandatory the payer can choose between online and offline. NO holding-limit figure is fixed in any adopted text.
signals.source_name: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, file 'digital euro' (updated 20/06/2026) for the ECON vote and counts; ECB RDG sixth progress report 06/07/2026 (citing Council general approach 19/12/2025 and ECON position 23/06/2026); press for the plenary and trilogue dates; Freshfields Technology Quotient for the divergence detail (press, uncorroborated)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every merchant acquirer and every mid/large merchant in AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG. (b) WHAT: IF the Council's 'payer can choose online or offline wherever acceptance is mandatory' line survives, it is the single most expensive sentence in the file for hardware — it would mean offline-capable acceptance devices (secure element, offline risk management) across the accepting estate rather than an app-only rollout. That conditional must be stated as a conditional until the Council text is read. Capped merchant fees compress acquirer margin and push acquirers toward lower-TCO outsourced/managed terminal estates — Printec's managed-services and TMS proposition. (c) WHEN: political agreement targeted end-2026, entry into force 2027, issuance targeted 2029; acceptance-estate capex commits in the 2027-2028 budget rounds.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that political agreement lands by end-2026; the holding limit remains genuinely open
signals.followup: PRIORITY: retrieve Council general approach texts ST-16695-2025 and ST-16696-2025 and the adopted EP mandate, and re-verify the online/offline-choice provision before any client-facing use — the entire hardware argument in this row hangs on it. Monitor the EP Legislative Train and Council press per trilogue. Do NOT quote any holding-limit figure until it appears in an adopted text or the Official Journal.
signals.verifier_note: PROCEDURAL DATES CONFIRMED from institutional sources: EP Legislative Train (updated 20/06/2026) confirms ECON 05/11/2025 and the 43-14-1 count and rapporteur Navarrete Rojas; the ECB progress report footnote 24 confirms the Council general approach of 19/12/2025 and states the ECON position of 23/06/2026. Plenary 09/07/2026 and trilogue 13/07/2026 confirmed by multiple press outlets, which ADD a vote count the original signal lacked: 416-169-22. One correction: the Council general approach was adopted under the DANISH Presidency; the Irish Presidency reference applies to the H2-2026 agreement target, which is plausible on rotation but was not verified from a Council source. THE SUBSTANTIVE DIVERGENCES REMAIN SINGLE-SOURCE LAW-FIRM ANALYSIS — the original signal presented them at the same confidence as the confirmed dates. I have relabelled them as reported-not-verified, because the 'implies' section leans entirely on the offline-choice line.

signals.entity: ECB — holding limit and cash funding/defunding (FAQ, primary)
signals.signal: CLOSES A BASELINE VERIFICATION DEBT — re-checked directly against the ECB FAQ. The FAQ states its technical analysis tested 'hypothetical holding limits of up to EUR 3,000 per person'. This is a MODELLED SCENARIO, not a decided or proposed legal limit; the figure repeated in Greek and other national press as 'the' cap has no legal basis. The FAQ further confirms, all verified verbatim: users can put money into a wallet 'via a linked bank account or by depositing cash'; 'anti-money laundering checks would be carried out by the distributing payment service provider (PSP) during the funding and defunding process, just as it is the case with cash withdrawals and deposits today'; offline payment details 'would be known only to the payer and the payee, providing a cash-like level of privacy'; the preparation phase launched November 2023 and concluded October 2025; the pilot starts H2-2027 and runs 12 months; and the Eurosystem aims 'to be ready for a potential first issuance of the digital euro during 2029, assuming the necessary regulation on the establishment of the digital euro is adopted in the course of 2026'. Secondary analyses place the cash funding/defunding duty in Article 13(3)(b) of the Commission proposal, obliging PSPs that already provide cash services to offer digital euro funding and defunding with banknotes and coins — this article reference was NOT re-verified against EUR-Lex this run.
signals.source_name: ECB — FAQs on the digital euro (primary, re-read 02/08/2026)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every euro-area credit institution operating ATMs or branch cash services — effectively all of them in the footprint. (b) WHAT: cash-to-digital-euro funding and defunding at the ATM is the hard hardware consequence. It requires ATM application changes (x-core, NCR APTRA), a wallet/NFC or QR interaction at the machine, and materially raises the value of DEPOSIT and RECYCLING ATMs over dispense-only ones, since cash-in to a wallet needs an intelligent-deposit or recycling module (NCR recyclers, Glory/Sesami TCRs). It also changes cash forecasting — an APTRA OptiCash story. Note the FAQ's AML framing: checks sit with the DISTRIBUTING PSP at funding and defunding, which is precisely the ATM/branch touchpoint. (c) WHEN: the obligation bites at issuance (targeted 2029) and dispense-only fleets take 2-3 years to refresh, so recycler/deposit business cases should be raised in 2027.
signals.likelihood: High on the funding/defunding duty; Medium on the final holding-limit level
signals.followup: Re-verify Article 13(3)(b) against the adopted text in the Official Journal once published — EUR-Lex was not re-fetched this run, so the article number is currently carried on secondary authority only. Build the ATM recycler business case tied to digital euro funding/defunding for the euro-area footprint banks. On the privacy/AML design questions clients will raise, state the ECB's published position only and refer interpretation to Printec's DPO / Compliance team rather than opining.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED verbatim on every FAQ element: the EUR 3,000 hypothetical, funding via linked account or cash deposit, AML at funding/defunding by the distributing PSP, cash-like offline privacy, preparation phase Nov-2023 to Oct-2025, pilot H2-2027 for 12 months, and the 2029 issuance conditional on adoption in 2026. The researcher's key judgement — that EUR 3,000 is a modelled scenario and not a legal cap — is correct and is the right reading of the source. The one unverified element is the Article 13(3)(b) citation, which remains on secondary authority; flagged in the signal text rather than dropped.

signals.entity: EU co-legislators — Regulation on the legal tender of euro banknotes and coins, 2023/0208(COD)
signals.country: EU euro area (AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG in footprint)
signals.signal: The legal-tender-of-cash Regulation travels in the SAME trilogue package as the digital euro. Per the EP Legislative Train file (last updated 20/06/2026): ECON adopted its position on the single currency package by 46 votes to 4 with 8 abstentions on 05/11/2025 (rapporteur Fernando Navarrete Rojas, PPE); the Council adopted its negotiating position in December 2025, with the cash regulation 'effectively prohibiting the refusal of cash except in narrowly defined cases'. Two limbs, both confirmed at that source: ACCEPTANCE — Member States must 'designate national competent authorities with oversight and regulatory powers to ensure acceptance and access to cash', and must submit annual assessments 'to the Commission and the ECB'; ACCESS — those assessments run against COMMON INDICATORS, and the new precision found on re-check is that these indicators are to be DEFINED THROUGH COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING ACTS, measuring cash acceptance levels and the 'density of cash access points in relation to the population'. The Council position also requires 'resilience measures to ensure the continuity of cash payments during major disruptions to electronic systems'. NOT FOUND at the cited source: the recital wording about the reduction of ATM networks creating risks to access to cash — do not attribute that quote to the Legislative Train page.
signals.source_name: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule — Scope and effects of legal tender of euro banknotes and coins (last updated 20/06/2026)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: ATM deployers and central banks of AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG. Greece, Croatia and Cyprus have seen the sharpest branch/ATM consolidation and are most exposed to a population-density access indicator. (b) WHAT: this is a floor under ATM demand at exactly the moment the digital euro is read as a threat to it. Member States failing their access indicators must add or protect access points — new ATMs and self-service kiosks, recyclers to keep rural machines stocked, and for the 'continuity during major disruptions to electronic systems' obligation, resilient offline-capable ATMs, device telemetry and monitoring, and cash optimisation (APTRA OptiCash) to evidence coverage. The annual national assessment creates a RECURRING evidence requirement that ATM telemetry data can serve — a subscription-shaped, not project-shaped, revenue line. (c) WHEN: agreement targeted end-2026 alongside the digital euro; competent authorities and the first assessment cycle follow within roughly 12-24 months of entry into force, so 2027-2028 budgets.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High — travels with the digital euro file under the same end-2026 target
signals.followup: The indicator methodology will be set by COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING ACT — that is the document to track, and it is the point at which ATM density thresholds become concrete and biddable. Obtain the ECON report and Council text; map Printec footprint ATM density against likely thresholds in GR, HR, CY and BG; position telemetry/monitoring as the compliance-evidence layer for the annual national assessment.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED at the cited EP source: the 46-4-8 ECON vote of 05/11/2025, rapporteur Navarrete Rojas, the December 2025 Council position, designation of national competent authorities, annual assessments to the Commission and the ECB, common indicators covering density of cash access points relative to population, and the resilience-during-disruption requirement. NEW PRECISION ADDED: the common indicators are to be defined through Commission implementing acts — the original signal omitted this, and it is the most commercially useful detail in the row because it identifies the document that will fix the thresholds. ONE ELEMENT CONTRADICTED AS TO SOURCING: the recital quote about ATM network reduction is not present on this page; it may originate in the 2023 Commission proposal recitals but was not verified there, so the attribution has been removed.

signals.entity: Digital Euro Regulation — provisions for non-euro-area Member States
signals.country: Romania, Czech Republic, Hungary (non-euro EU footprint)
signals.signal: [STANDING — provisions dated to the 2023 Commission proposal; not re-verified against a primary text this run.] The proposed Regulation contains specific provisions for Member States whose currency is not the euro: PSPs incorporated in a non-euro-area Member State may offer digital euro payment services to euro-area residents by free provision of services or freedom of establishment, subject to specific obligations and to supervision by the competent authorities of that non-euro Member State; residents outside the euro area may access the digital euro by opening accounts with PSPs in an EEA country, or in a third country subject to a prior EU agreement and/or arrangements concluded between the ECB and the national central bank concerned. Romania's euro-adoption target (ERM II 2026 / euro 2029) is widely assessed as unrealistic given the fiscal deficit; Czechia and Hungary have no adoption date. TREAT AS BACKGROUND: neither the provisions nor the adoption-target assessment were re-checked against OEIL, EUR-Lex or the national central banks in this run.
signals.source_name: European Parliament OEIL document summary for 2023/0212(COD) (cited by the original researcher; NOT re-fetched this run)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: BCR, BRD, Banca Transilvania, Raiffeisen Romania (RO); CSOB, Komercni banka, Ceska sporitelna (CZ); OTP, K&H, Erste Hungary (HU). (b) WHAT: no mandatory acceptance obligation in RO/CZ/HU. Banks that want to distribute cross-border, or whose euro-area parents standardise a group-wide stack, would still need certified acceptance and wallet components — but this is a follow-on wave, not a 2027 spend. Note the group-standardisation channel is the realistic near-term route, since RBI, Erste and OTP parents are all exposed to the euro-area programme. (c) WHEN: post-2029 unless an ECB-NCB arrangement is concluded earlier. Near-term regulatory spend in RO/CZ/HU stays with instant payments and VoP.
signals.likelihood: Low that RO/CZ/HU banks spend on digital euro before 2029
signals.followup: Re-fetch the OEIL summary or the proposal articles on non-euro-area Member States next run to confirm the provisions and correct the dating. Watch for any ECB arrangement with BNR, CNB or MNB. Keep RO/CZ/HU account plans anchored on the instant-payments/VoP deadline rather than the digital euro — and verify that deadline independently, as it was carried over from another workstream and not checked here.
signals.verifier_note: NOT INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED — the OEIL summary was not re-fetched this run, so the substance rests on the original researcher's reading. signals.signal: [STANDING — NBU e-hryvnia page as retrieved 02/08/2026; project launched September 2021.] Re-verified directly against the NBU's own page. The project remains at design/research stage with NO pilot date published. The NBU is 'considering and processing the following possible options for using the e-hryvnia that will shape its design and main features: the e-hryvnia for retail noncash payments with the options for programmed targeted money; the e-hryvnia in the circulation of virtual assets; the e-hryvnia for cross-border payments' — confirmed verbatim. Design features confirmed verbatim: wallet access restorable through another financial institution using DLT (distributed ledger technology); OFFLINE PAYMENTS where either the payer or the payee lacks a connection to the e-hryvnia platform, with the case of both parties offline also under consideration; programmability (splitting a payment across several payers, conditional and recurring payments); and 'the option to provide targeted government aid, regardless of merchants and payment service providers'. The term e-hryvnia is defined in the Law of Ukraine On Payment Services; if approved it would be legal tender and exist only in cashless form. Published artefacts are the Analytical Report on the E-hryvnia Pilot Project, the CBDCinUA conference report and a survey on the possibility of e-hryvnia implementation — no 2026-dated milestone appears on the page. Press suggestions of NBU doubts about introduction by 2027 on wartime cost grounds are NOT stated on the NBU site.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — E-hryvnia (official page, bank.gov.ua), retrieved 02/08/2026
signals.implies: (a) WHO: PrivatBank, Oschadbank, Raiffeisen Ukraine, Monobank/Universal and the NBU. (b) WHAT: nothing to buy yet. The two design points that would eventually create Printec demand are offline payments and targeted state aid delivered 'regardless of merchants and payment service providers' — aid delivered outside the merchant/PSP chain would still have to be cashed out or spent somewhere, which points at ATM and POS acceptance in a market where Printec already supplies NCR recyclers to PrivatBank. (c) WHEN: no committed date; Ukrainian bank payments capex in 2026-2027 goes to SEP ISO 20022 and EU-accession alignment, not CBDC. Watch item, not pipeline.
signals.likelihood: Low that an e-hryvnia pilot goes live within 12 months
signals.followup: Poll the NBU news feed quarterly for an e-hryvnia technology-partner selection or pilot announcement — that is the trigger. ACCESS NOTE: bank.gov.ua returns HTTP 403 to plain fetch tools; retrieved successfully with a desktop browser User-Agent via curl (HTTP 200), so this source is reachable and should not be dropped in future runs.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED against the primary source, retrieved after a 403 by retrying with a desktop User-Agent per the access playbook. All three use-case options and all four design features match the NBU page near-verbatim, as does the September 2021 launch, the Law on Payment Services definition, the legal-tender-if-approved and cashless-only framing, and the list of published artefacts. The absence of any pilot date is confirmed. The researcher's caution that the wartime-cost press narrative is not on the NBU site is correct and well handled.

signals.signal: [STANDING — pilot closed 03/02/2025.] Hungary has NO live CBDC programme and no digital forint launch decision, design document or 2026 timeline could be found. UPGRADED TO PRIMARY SOURCING with corrected dates: the MNB's retail CBDC pilot was the Student Safe (Diákszéf) mobile application, run with the Money Compass Foundation. Corrections to the original signal — the programme was launched in 2020 as the MNB Digital Student Safe and RENEWED as a CBDC-based app in 2023 (not launched in 2023), and its public operation ENDED ON 03/02/2025, the MNB describing it as a scheduled closure to free capacity for analytical work. The MNB published its own press release marking the end of the pilot and a full white paper on the project on 03/03/2025. The pilot won the Central Banking Publications 'CBDC Initiative of the Year' award in 2024. CBDC trackers accordingly record Hungary as having moved backwards from pilot to research. The MNB continues to examine the preconditions for central bank digital money; no MNB rendelet (decree) on CBDC was identified.
signals.source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank — press release 'Student Safe mobile app says goodbye – the MNB's successful pilot project comes to an end' and MNB white paper 'Student Safe: the Magyar Nemzeti Bank's retail central bank digital currency pilot' (03/03/2025)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: OTP, K&H, Erste Hungary, MBH. (b) WHAT: nothing on CBDC. Hungarian bank regulatory spend in 2026-2027 goes to instant payments/VoP, NIS2 audits and accessibility, not to a digital forint. (c) WHEN: n/a. Report as a NEGATIVE finding so account teams do not chase a phantom digital forint programme — and note that the closure gives Printec a factual counter to any competitor pitching 'CBDC readiness' in Hungary.
signals.likelihood: Very low — no MNB programme in flight; the only retail pilot was closed in February 2025
signals.followup: Sweep the MNB Hungarian-language sajtóközlemények page quarterly for 'digitális jegybankpénz'. The MNB white paper of 03/03/2025 is the authoritative account of what was tried and why it stopped — worth reading before any Hungarian CBDC conversation.
signals.verifier_note: CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED (no live Hungarian CBDC programme) but the SOURCING AND DATES WERE WRONG and are now corrected. The original row rested on an aggregator (HRF CBDC Tracker, undated '2025') and was rated Low; MNB primary sources exist and were located — an MNB press release announcing the pilot's end and an MNB white paper dated 03/03/2025 — so tier rises to primary, date to 03/03/2025, confidence to Medium. Corrected facts: the programme began in 2020 as MNB Digital Student Safe and was renewed in 2023, not launched in 2023; public operation ended 03/02/2025, not vaguely 'until 2025'. is_new set true because the row's sourcing and dates changed materially.

signals.signal: [STANDING — most recent CNB item is a commentary on the digital euro dated 06/09/2025.] The CNB Bank Board has taken NO decision on issuing a Czech CBDC — verbatim on the CNB site: 'Bankovní rada ČNB dosud nepřijala žádné rozhodnutí ve věci případné emise českých CBDC' [The CNB Bank Board has so far taken no decision on the possible issuance of Czech CBDC]. The CNB established a CBDC working group in February 2021; its main published output remains 'Digitální peníze centrálních bank' [Central bank digital money] of 08/11/2022. The CNB's position is that any introduction must be preceded by 'důkladné vyhodnocení jejich potřebnosti a přidané hodnoty' [a thorough evaluation of their necessity and added value] plus public debate, and it warns of risks to monetary policy implementation and financial stability, notably that a CBDC could withdraw a significant volume of bank deposits. DECISIVE ADDITIONAL BARRIER found on re-check and absent from the original signal: a LEGISLATIVE CHANGE would be required, because current Czech law does not permit the CNB to issue CBDC. No digital koruna timeline exists.
signals.source_name: Česká národní banka — «Digitální peníze centrálních bank (CBDC)» [Central bank digital money (CBDC)], incl. CNB commentary on the digital euro dated 06/09/2025 and the working-group output of 08/11/2022
signals.implies: (a) WHO: Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, Komerční banka, Moneta. (b) WHAT: nothing on CBDC. Czech bank regulatory spend stays on instant payments/VoP, accessibility and DORA. (c) WHEN: n/a. Strongest use is as a competitive counter-message: a vendor pitching 'CBDC readiness' in Czechia is selling against the CNB's own published scepticism AND against a statutory bar that would require a change in Czech law before issuance is even possible.
signals.likelihood: Very low — no decision, published scepticism, and a legal bar requiring legislative change
signals.followup: Re-check the CNB CBDC page and blog annually. The trigger to watch is the Czech euro-adoption debate, not a domestic CBDC. Note the CNB has a dated commentary on the DIGITAL EURO (06/09/2025) — worth reading, since a Czech euro-adoption debate would pull Czech banks into the digital euro acceptance perimeter.
signals.verifier_note: CONFIRMED on the CNB's own page, including the 'no decision' sentence in the original Czech. TWO IMPROVEMENTS over the original row: (1) RECENCY — the original dated the row Nov-2022; the CNB page carries a more recent dated item, a commentary on the digital euro of 06/09/2025, so the row is re-dated and is less stale than presented; (2) a substantive fact the original missed — Czech law does not currently permit CBDC issuance, so legislative change is a precondition. This strengthens rather than weakens the researcher's conclusion. Working group founded February 2021.

signals.signal: [STANDING — NBS statement dated 26/01/2023, NOT 2026.] Serbia has not reached a decision stage on a CBDC and there is no official timeline for a digital dinar. Re-verified against an NBS primary page rather than the aggregator originally cited: the NBS states it is in a phase of consideration and analysis, monitors global CBDC developments and exchanges experience with other central banks, and points to its IPS instant payment system — operational since October 2018 and, the NBS notes, launched a week before the ECB's equivalent — as evidence that 24/7 real-time payments and mobile banking already meet the need. The NBS also distinguishes the Law on Digital Assets, which regulates privately issued virtual currencies and expressly does NOT regulate the issuance of central bank digital currency. The NBS undertakes to 'regularly and timely inform the public of its activities in this sphere'. IMPORTANT RECENCY CAVEAT: the authoritative NBS statement is over three years old and no 2026 NBS position was found, so the original row's framing as a 2026 position is not supported. Claims on Serbian technology blogs that a digital dinar is already being tested on a permissioned DLT with named commercial-bank validators could NOT be corroborated on nbs.rs and should not be relied upon.

signals.entity: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) and Central Bank of Kosovo (BQK) — unilaterally euroised economies
signals.signal: Montenegro (since 2002) and Kosovo use the euro unilaterally with no monetary agreement with the EU, no Eurosystem seat and no access to ECB liquidity facilities. Under the Digital Euro Regulation as proposed, residents and businesses outside the euro area can access the digital euro only through PSPs in an EEA state, or in a third country subject to a prior EU agreement and/or an arrangement between the ECB and the relevant national central bank — so neither CBCG nor BQK would automatically obtain digital euro access or distribution rights. Bloomberg reported on 04/05/2026 that Montenegro says the EU is working to resolve the unilateral euro-use issue hindering its accession, with an EU proposal expected by end-May 2026; the article is PAYWALLED, so its headline and date are confirmed to exist but the substance was not read, and no primary EU source confirming the proposal or its outcome was found. Secondary commentary suggests the workaround under discussion would define the regime as an unorthodox fixed-rate currency arrangement within the accession treaty — this is commentary, not an EU text, and must not be presented as EU policy. SUB-CLAIMS NOT RE-CHECKED THIS RUN: SEPA geographical admission of Montenegro and Albania in November 2024, and the Montenegro TIPS-clone go-live of 20/07/2026 with all 11 banks.
signals.source_name: European Commission — The euro outside the euro area (standing primary page, undated for this purpose); Bloomberg, 'Montenegro Says EU Working to Fix Euro Issue Hindering Accession', 04/05/2026 (paywalled, headline/date only)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: CBCG and Montenegro's banks; BQK and Kosovo's banks (NLB, ProCredit, Raiffeisen Kosovo, TEB). (b) WHAT: if an EU-Montenegro monetary arrangement lands, Montenegrin banks would face digital euro acceptance obligations on a euro-area clock from a much thinner infrastructure base — terminals, ATM software, certification and managed services bought as one package. If it does not, these markets stay on cards and instant payments. Either way both are already spending on instant-payment and SEPA acceptance, which is the addressable business today. (c) WHEN: unknowable until an EU proposal is public — 2027+ optionality, not forecastable pipeline.
signals.likelihood: Medium that the EU tables something on Montenegrin euro use within 12 months; Low that it produces digital euro obligations before 2029
signals.followup: OPERATOR REQUEST: the Bloomberg article of 04/05/2026 is paywalled and needs a licensed read. Track DG ECFIN and Montenegro accession chapter 17 (economic and monetary policy) for the euro-use proposal from a primary EU source — the end-May 2026 expectation has now passed with no confirmed outcome found, which is itself worth chasing. Ask CBCG whether digital euro features in its 2027 work programme. Re-check the SEPA and TIPS-clone sub-claims before use.
signals.verifier_note: MIXED. The Bloomberg article's existence, exact headline and 04/05/2026 date are CONFIRMED, but it is paywalled so the substance is unread — the 'EU proposal expected by end of May 2026' is therefore secondhand, and critically, no primary EU source confirming that a proposal was tabled or what it said could be found, even though end-May 2026 is now two months past. SOURCING DEFECT CORRECTED: the original row put a Bloomberg date (04/05/2026) on a European Commission standing page URL, implying Commission authority for a press claim; tier lowered from primary to press and the two sources separated. The euroisation background is uncontroversial. Confidence stays Low, correctly.
